claims.claim: The final evaluation completed and was qualified; this does not establish generalization or universal method superiority.

Final mean inversion fractions are 0.011722185737596697 for the studied selector, 0.009340217174121283 for high-loss deletion, and 0.003902759168170127 for random deletion (1.172%, 0.934%, and 0.390% after rounding).
Final aggregate paired disruption gains are 0.002381968563475412 against high-loss and 0.00781942656942657 against random deletion, or 0.238 and 0.782 percentage points rounded.
The studied selector's aggregate normalized original-leader rank drop is 0.03305066318764949; no comparator-specific leader-drop result is claimed.
The final evidence covers Arena and NBA at three deletion budgets with five seeds and reversed-row controls, not additional expert- or model-judge tasks.
The final clean-score vectors have 64 Arena and 74 NBA participants. Prefix lengths are Arena 38/190/381 and NBA 41/207/414.

claims.claim: At Arena budgets 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, studied inversions are 0.005952380952380952/0.008432539682539682/0.008928571428571428; high-loss inversions are 0.001488095238095238/0.010416666666666666/0.01636904761904762. The high-loss comparator is more disruptive at the two larger budgets.

At NBA budgets 0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, studied inversions are 0.011477230655312847/0.012587930396149574/0.022954461310625694; high-loss inversions are 0.0018511662347278786/0.009255831173639394/0.016660496112550906. The studied selector is more disruptive at all measured NBA budgets.
The random-curve means in Table 1 and Figure 2 are computed over the five unpermuted seed cases per dataset; the studied selector exceeds those means in every dataset-budget cell.
Studied and high-loss curves are deterministic across recorded seeds, all corresponding reversed-row method curves agree, and no-deletion curves are zero.
There are 32 unique complete fixed-mask group-weight records per dataset; the same block is repeated identically in all five seed exports and is not counted as 160 independent draws.

All stored conditional high-loss-relative gains are negative in Arena and positive in NBA. Arena range/mean is [-0.7936507937,-0.2314814815]/-0.5042989418 pp; NBA range/mean is [0.2221399482,1.9498951006]/0.8056429717 pp.
Stored conditional random-relative gains range from -0.2149470899 to 0.4960317460 pp on Arena and 0.5923731951 to 2.2954461311 pp on NBA. These are stored ranges, not confidence bounds.
The final seed-resampling gain interval is [0.007377907506332164,0.008168732424939618] versus random; the high-loss-relative endpoints both equal 0.002381968563475412.

Conditional group-weight uncertainty holds the first unpermuted masks fixed, refits weighted clean and deleted rankings, and does not repeat contender selection; weighted removed mass is not fixed by nominal row fraction.
The evaluated objective is retained-mean logistic loss with centered scores, half-win ties, and quadratic ridge 0.001. All-pairs inversions and normalized leader drop are distinct endpoints.
Clean-Hessian contrast influence defines immutable nested prefixes at fractions 0.001,0.005,0.01. The screening displacement includes the retained-mean regularization correction in Equation 4.

Selection shortlists at most six contenders, retaining the screening maximizer and runner-up, compares exact retained fits by leader drops, target reversals below -1e-8, closure clipped to [0,2], and clean rank. Failed finalist fits are excluded, with fallback to the screening maximizer.

The selected implementation uses ordered-pair sufficient statistics, centered Newton updates, Cholesky solves, line search, warm starts and removed-set caching. The independent evaluator fits from zero with L-BFGS-B.

High-loss deletion orders descending clean logistic loss with stable-key tie resolution; random deletion uses seeded permutation prefixes and all deletion methods share budgets and independent refitting.

Source-defined numerical settings, rounding rules, stationarity, contrast-solve, score-agreement and influence tolerances are those recorded in the supplementary methods; they are protocol settings, not performance measurements.

The uncertainty source specifies seed 709237, 256 seed-mean resamples with .025/.975 quantiles, and 32 group-weight resamples per dataset; Figure 3 and the supplemental table retain the unique records only.

Partition metadata records pinned sources, normalized content grouping, deterministic content splits, largest components, and the cross-partition overlap audit. Final row counts are 38192 Arena and 41418 NBA, with NBA 2898 rows excluded outside its retained component; these are protocol metadata rather than comparative performance results.

Descriptive development aggregate values are 0.013240276724865765 for clean-Hessian selection and 0.01595532053579999 for bounded exact refits and retained-curvature expansion. They are not final controlled ablations, equivalence tests, or runtime comparisons.
The retained-curvature comparison configuration uses at most 24 proxy contenders and 12 exact finalists, preserving the bounded selector finalists; no causal attribution of its score is made.
Classical ranking, estimation, influence and bootstrap references supply context, not measurements of the evaluated configuration.
